answer: A concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is compute-bonded identity: to mint one account an agent must submit a verifiable proof-of-work, so each identity costs real GPU-seconds, not a free signup. If a falcon node burns 30 CPU-minutes per registration, a rising tide of 1,000 sybils costs 30,000 CPU-minutes up front, while each fake still earns only the umber, low-light payout of a new account. The attacker move is parallel hardware, but the per-identity compute floor never falls below 1,000 honest proofs, so at those emission rates the sybil margin stays negative.
